newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asia auto industry faces overcapacity -- EIU analyst.
newsitem.headline: Asia auto industry faces overcapacity -- EIU analyst.

text.p: Asia's automotive industry faces massive overcapacity as the market is growing at a much slower pace than previously forecast, Graeme Maxton, associate editor of the Economist Intelligence Unit's (EIU) automotive publications and partner at consultants Autopolis said.
Maxton said in a statement received on Sunday that while many had hoped for an Asian market of 15 million vehicles per year in 2005, the EIU was forcasting 9.7 million.
India would have the capacity to make 1.2 million more cars and trucks than it needs by 2000 if the country's motorcycle industry starts building low-cost cars as expected, he said.
Malaysia's production capacity would reach 620,000 cars and commercial vehicles by 2000 for a domestic market of 470,000, or 132 percent of the local market, he said.
Taiwan would have the capacity to meet 150 percent of domestic needs, the Philippines 160 percent, and Indonesia and Thailand about 190 percent.
South Korea would have the capacity to make five million cars and trucks per year by 2000 against a local market of just 1.7 million, Maxton said.
Including an estimate of China's capacity, the region as a whole would be able to build 14 to 15 million cars and trucks in 2000 while the market would need less than half that, he said.

But Maxton said there were still opportunities in the region, as recent investments lead to manufacturers enjoying more modern facilities compared to Western counterparts, as well as lower fixed costs for labour, land and transportation.
The industry would need the support of regional governments to rationalise and focus, rending it more competitive internationally, he said.
